title: RevealX ransomware and C2 detections
volume: None on a normal day. Each detection update from RevealX makes one detection, in the source device's case.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Two custom detection rules for ExtraHop RevealX, on the third-party alert records the library's RevealX parser writes from detection webhooks. They make a detection when RevealX sees ransomware activity, and when it scores C2 beaconing High risk. Each rule matches sensor type ExtraHop RevealX only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's RevealX parser, and send detections to HTTP Ingest from a notification rule with the one-line payload in the parser entry's README. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parser writes the detection type as the alert category and maps the risk score to severity in ExtraHop's bands: 80 and above is High.
- The ransomware rule takes Ransomware Activity at any risk score. The beaconing rule takes beaconing detection types at High only.
- Brute force and recon detection types aren't taken.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 5 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 27 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take.
- The detections went to HTTP Ingest one per request as JSON, as the custom webhook sends them.

Known gaps:
- With Send for every detection update, RevealX posts each update, so one ongoing detection can make several.
- src is the device that started the traffic, which for a C2 detection is the victim, not the attacker.
